solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ruffled cook concealing what's bad

indicators.note: something concealing another holds it out of sight inside itself

parts.note: to fry is to cook in fat
ill as a noun is harm or evil

explanation.surface: A flustered cook is hiding something nasty from the diners.
explanation.definitionFit: Frilly clothing is trimmed with ruffles, gathered strips of fabric.

clue.text: Supporting fashionable position, say

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
what is in is in fashion
a stance is a position taken

explanation.surface: Someone backs whatever view is currently trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the last word: 'say' introduces an example, just as the answer phrase does.
explanation.definitionFit: Both 'say' and the answer phrase are used to introduce an illustrative example.

clue.text: Change again as dieter taking new course

indicators.note: taking a new course means heading off in a different direction, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A slimmer switches to a different diet plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-edit a text is to revise or alter it a second time.

clue.text: Immigrant in one ship that is heading north

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A newcomer travels aboard a vessel bound northward.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the 'that is' abbreviation is reversed. The answer is a Japanese word for a first-generation Japanese immigrant to the Americas.
explanation.definitionFit: An Issei is a first-generation Japanese emigrant, especially one settled in the USA.

clue.text: Part of chemical to be effective in upsetting sickness

indicators.note: one element is placed inside the other
upsetting something tips it over, so in a down entry the word is turned upside down

parts.note: mal is French-derived for illness, as in mal de mer
a drug is said to act when it takes effect

explanation.surface: A component of some compound gets to work when it upsets the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: The sickness word is turned over first, then the acting word goes inside it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lactam is a cyclic amide, a structural group found in chemicals such as penicillin.

clue.text: Nasty headless bogey to disappear, as before?

definitions.note: the answer is the archaic past participle, 'gone'

indicators.note: something nasty is twisted out of its proper shape, so the letters are rearranged
without a head means the opening letter is lost

explanation.surface: A ghastly goblin with no head is told to vanish, as in the old tales.
explanation.walkthrough: Ygoe is Spenser's word for 'gone', so the definition means having disappeared in former usage; 'as before' flags the obsolete form.
explanation.definitionFit: Ygoe is an archaic past participle of go, meaning departed or vanished.

clue.text: A crowd round edge of village with a basic form of life

indicators.note: going round something encloses it
the edge of a word is one of its end letters, here the final one

explanation.surface: A throng gathers at the village boundary, along with a primitive creature.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoeba is a single-celled organism, a textbook example of the simplest kind of life.

clue.text: A mother in charge of father initially

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A mother takes charge of the household's father at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The father in question is the first one of all, Adam, so 'of father initially' means 'relating to Adam'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamic means relating to Adam, in Genesis the first man and father of humankind.

clue.text: In short time a small egg is seen as sacred object

indicators.note: one part is set inside the other

parts.note: a nit is the tiny egg of a louse

explanation.surface: Briefly, a tiny egg comes to be revered as holy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' and the louse egg go together inside MO.
explanation.definitionFit: A manito (manitou) is an Algonquian spirit or the object or fetish in which it resides, held sacred.

clue.text: Silver coin the French female put in bowl

parts.note: the écu was an old French silver coin

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman drops a silver coin into a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: An écuelle is a two-handled French porringer or soup bowl.

clue.text: Soup bishop tipped over in riotous social occasion?

indicators.note: tipping over turns things upside down, so in a down entry the order runs backwards

parts.note: a purée is a thick blended soup
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop spills his soup at a rowdy party.
explanation.walkthrough: A beer-up is Australian slang for a drinking party.
explanation.definitionFit: A beer-up is an Australian slang term for a boisterous drinking session.

clue.text: Gathering for men being old, lacking energy in posture

indicators.note: one part is placed inside the other
lacking means going without, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An all-male event is getting on, its participants drained of energy in their bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag event is one for men only, as in stag party.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag dance is a dance attended by men only, with no women partners.

clue.text: Growling maiden in unrestrained display of temper about to be restrained

indicators.note: the first part goes inside the second

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: being restrained means being held in, so this part goes inside another

parts.note: to make a scene is to have an angry outburst

explanation.surface: A young woman snarls in an angry outburst that has to be reined in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growling' is the definition, though it reads as describing the maiden; 'about' is circa, a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fremescence is a rare word for a murmuring or growling noise, from Latin fremere, to roar.

clue.text: Letter just produced, first off

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off and discarded

explanation.surface: A letter has only just been written, and the first one is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter is from the Hebrew alphabet, not a piece of mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Resh is the twentieth letter of the Hebrew alphabet.

clue.text: Roman boy in dog's mess?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Latin word for a boy
second meaning: dog dung, once collected for tanning leather

explanation.surface: A Roman lad has stepped in something a dog left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Tanners used dog dung, called puer or pure, to treat hides.
explanation.definitionFit: Puer is Latin for boy, and in English also a name for dog dung used in tanning.

clue.text: Imagine identity getting almost eroded

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an ID is proof of identity

explanation.surface: Picture someone's sense of self being nearly worn away.
explanation.definitionFit: To ideate is to form ideas or conceive of something in the mind.

clue.text: Bid made by mean person wanting minimum of expenditure

parts.note: a miser is a stingy person

indicators.note: the least possible amount of a word is its single opening letter

explanation.surface: A stingy person keeps spending to the absolute minimum when bidding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' means needing here, not lacking: nothing is taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: Misère is a card-game bid undertaking to lose every trick.

clue.text: I cut a lump out — a flowery cluster

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener slices a chunk off a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A capitulum is a dense head of small flowers, as in a daisy or thistle.

clue.text: Old cut offered by markets rejected — a trick!

indicators.note: rejected things are sent back, so the letters are read in reverse

explanation.surface: Turned away from the markets, a piece of meat turns out to be a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old cut' is not meat: it is an obsolete fencing term.
explanation.definitionFit: A stramaçon is an old term for a slashing stroke with the edge of a sword.

clue.text: Applaud Information Technology incorporating the latest in slick software

indicators.note: incorporating means taking inside, so one letter is held within the rest

parts.note: to root for someone is to cheer them on

indicators.note: the most recent arrival in a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Cheer the IT department for embracing the newest slick program.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Applaud' and 'Information Technology' together form the container; the inserted letter lands at their join.
explanation.definitionFit: A rootkit is malicious software that gains hidden administrator-level access to a computer.

clue.text: Gloom once of daughter, brought up inadequately

indicators.note: not adequately means falling short, so the final letter is missing

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
to rear children is to bring them up

explanation.surface: A daughter's gloomy past comes from a poor upbringing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks an archaic word: dreare is Spenser's form of drear.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreare is an obsolete noun meaning dreariness or gloom.

clue.text: Is woman diminished without kids?

explanation.surface: A woman wonders whether she is lessened by having no children.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal and formal word for offspring, so issueless means childless.

clue.text: Everyone must wear fixed helmet

indicators.note: something worn wraps around the wearer, so one part sits inside the other

explanation.surface: A safety rule: all personnel must wear a secured helmet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sallet is a light medieval helmet, often with a neck guard.

clue.text: Old farm animal slaughtered for Easter

indicators.note: slaughtered means hacked about, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A beast from the farm is killed for the Easter feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' flags an obsolete spelling of steer.
explanation.definitionFit: Steare is an old spelling of steer, a young castrated bullock.

clue.text: Liveliness of goblin, character ultimately making maximum ascent

indicators.note: in a down entry, the final letter climbing as far as it can puts it right at the top

parts.note: a sprite is a goblin or elf

explanation.surface: An imp climbs as high as it can, full of spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of the goblin word moves from the bottom of the column to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is French-derived for spirit, wit and liveliness.

clue.text: Instruments from India borne by celebrities

indicators.note: something borne is carried within, so one letter is held inside another word

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Famous people bring musical instruments over from India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from India' looks like a description of the instruments, but India gives only one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitars are long-necked stringed Indian instruments.

clue.text: A new atomiser for perfume

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters are remade into another order

explanation.surface: Buying a fresh spray bottle for one's scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perfume' is a verb here, not the scent itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To aromatise is to give something a fragrance, which is what perfuming does.

clue.text: Happened to get love — a relief?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Finding love at last comes as a relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relief' means a carved raised design, not a feeling of ease.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a gem or shell carved in relief, the design raised against a contrasting background.

clue.text: Clear the foreign weed?

parts.note: nett profit is what is cleared after costs

explanation.surface: An instruction to clear away a weed from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The nettle is a stinging plant commonly treated as a garden weed, hence the question mark for an example.

clue.text: Sign on vehicle recently parked outside Public Library

indicators.note: a car parked outside a building stands around its front, so one part goes round the other

parts.note: late can mean recently, as in 'of late'
PL is the abbreviation for Public Library

explanation.surface: A car with a sign was recently left outside the public library.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an L-plate is the red L on white displayed by a learner driver.
explanation.definitionFit: An L-plate is the plate marking a car driven by a learner, a sign on the vehicle.

clue.text: Rare game with large number getting no score

parts.note: a lot is a large number

explanation.surface: A rarely played game in which most players fail to score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare' marks this as an uncommon spelling of a familiar game.
explanation.definitionFit: Loto is a less common spelling of lotto, the numbers game like bingo.

clue.text: Bird lacking right food

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a crake is a bird of the rail family
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A bird is without the proper food.
explanation.definitionFit: Cake is a baked sweet foodstuff, so it is a kind of food.

clue.text: Agent with ingratiating manner

indicators.note: with here means contained within, so the answer sits inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A spy who wins people over with a smarmy charm.
explanation.walkthrough: G-man is American slang for an FBI agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A G-man, short for government man, is an agent of the US Federal Bureau of Investigation.

clue.text: Flow of water seen in journey around one green

indicators.note: one word goes around the others, enclosing them

explanation.surface: A stream is spotted on a trip round a village green.
explanation.definitionFit: A river tide is the tidal current in a river, a flow of water up or downstream.

clue.text: Tiny bird in waste water

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A little bird splashes about in dirty water.
explanation.definitionFit: Petite means small and dainty, especially of a woman's build.

clue.text: Redundant old site, derelict, containing nothing

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one letter goes within the other word
something derelict is ruined and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An abandoned old site with nothing on it is surplus to requirements.
explanation.definitionFit: Otiose means serving no practical purpose, so superfluous or redundant.
